chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a Christian man who had converted to Islam, and with him was a pig that he had roasted and seasoned with basil. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What compelled you to do this?' The man said: 'I was sick, so I craved the meat.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What about the meat of the goat?' And it was following him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you had eaten it, I would have established the Hadd (fixed penalty) upon you, but I will strike you with a strike so that you do not return.' So he struck him until his urine trickled out.
ai.seo_question: What was the ruling and punishment for a convert who ate pork in the time of Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *Adab* (discipline) versus *Hadd* (fixed punishment) in early Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (AS) chose corporal punishment to deter the convert's specific craving rather than imposing the full legal penalty for pork consumption. The narrative highlights the Imam's pedagogical approach, using the availability of goat meat to question the convert's preference and administering a strike until he urinated, a sign of physical exhaustion or submission, to ensure the lesson was internalized. This incident is often cited by scholars to demonstrate the flexibility of judicial discretion (*Ra'y*) in applying punishments based on context and individual circumstances.
